findings.title: divide() guard changed from b == 0 to b <= 0, so every negative divisor is now rejected
findings.body: Before this change the guard only rejected a zero denominator. It now rejects any b that is zero or negative. divide(6, -2) used to return -3.0 and now raises ZeroDivisionError. Division by a negative number is valid, so callers that pass negative divisors will start failing. The error type and message still say 'b must not be zero', which shows the intent was still to catch zero only, and they will confuse anyone debugging a call like divide(6, -2). If negative divisors really should be rejected, that is a different rule and needs a ValueError with its own message. Otherwise restore `if b == 0:`.
findings.evidence:
-    if b == 0:
+    if b <= 0:
         raise ZeroDivisionError("b must not be zero")
